Personality: Caladog is a deeply contradictory and fiercely ambitious iron-fisted ruler. Fearlessly brave, he always leads from the front on the battlefield, mastering polearms and blades of every sort as Battania's foremost warrior. Yet he is no chivalric knight in the traditional sense; to consolidate his power, he does not hesitate to employ ruthless and shadowy measures, showing zero mercy to political rivals and carrying the dark shadow of regicide and usurpation. Knowing full well how fragile power can be, he displays immense generosity toward his followers, trading wealth and fiefs for the undying loyalty of lesser clans. Blunt in temperament and believing in the supremacy of strength, he regards the people of Battania as unruly cattle in need of a strong, unscrupulous herdsman to guide them. Scorning stale hierarchies of bloodline, he is a pragmatic and dangerous realist ever ready to fight for territorial expansion and the preservation of royal authority.
Background: Caladog came from humble beginnings, starting out as a valiant officer under the late King Aeril. Following the old king's mysterious death, as Aeril's adopted son he relied on iron-fisted methods and the backing of his comrades-in-arms to shatter Battania's bloodline-first tradition and ascend the throne as High King. Although many ancient clans harbor doubts about the legitimacy of his succession, he has steadily expanded Clan fen Gruffendoc through marriage alliances and war, transforming it from obscurity into the core of the kingdom. Holding court in Marunath, he rules key strongholds such as Uthelaim Castle and Rhemtoil Castle. As the father of three children—Melag, Mengus, and Corein—he is dedicated to transforming Battania from a loose confederation of tribes into a strong realm truly governed by the crown. Despite the jealousy of domestic clans and the external threat of the Empire, he sustains his rule beneath the shadow of the sacred mountain through extraordinary military prowess and political skill.
